newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end down sharply to limit on slow cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end down sharply to limit on slow cash.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed sharply lower in limitless January and with March down the daily $10.00 per tbf limit as long liquidation developed on slow cash trade to touch off sell stops, traders said.
Limitless January ended $21.90 per tbf lower at $411.80 while March remained locked down the daily limit at $419.70 per tbf. Other months finished $9.70 to $2.90 per tbf lower.

General selling prompted by slow cash trade, overbought conditions and weather-reduced construction pessured futures. Mills had been hedging in futures for days prompting ideas cash was not be as strong as futures had reflected, they said.
"If the mills were selling in the futures they didn't have much confidence in the cash, said Curt Cunningham, President Pacific Futures Trading.
"Inquiries (at mills) have never resulted in firm orders and the reload operators and distributors with wood are finding it tough to sell," Cunningham added.
He also noted that wholesalers are selling lumber at $400 while mills are asking between $420 and $425.
Further sharp losses are seen Wednesday as March traded synthetically in options at $412, down $7.70 per tbf.
